literature.headline_zh: 人肠道病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人肠道病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 该综述的结论是,人类干细胞衍生的培养物、类器官、气液界面系统和组合体通过模仿人体组织结构、细胞复杂性和 宿主 反应,显着改善了 NPEV 发病机制 的研究。这些模型对于了解病毒趋向性、受体使用、组织特异性易感性和遗传变异至关重要。 [10.1128/jvi.01699-25]
肠道病毒 D68 感染后,miR-3156-1 的初级和成熟形式上调。研究发现 miR-3156-3p 直接靶向 K+ 通道相关基因的 3'-非翻译区,导致质膜去极化和 Ca2+ 流入,从而增加病毒释放。在 ICR 新生小鼠模型中,预先施用 miR-3156-3p antagomir 可减少病毒相关的急性弛缓性麻痹。 [10.1016/j.ymthe.2026.09.038]
从蒙大拿州黑柿中提取的 CID 101282068 显示出预测的结合亲和力,对接分数为 -9.8 kcal/mol,Gbind = -33.27 kcal/mol。它还在低聚界面处与关键残基保持了最高数量的持久氢键。 [10.3390/biophysica6050096]
所有衍生物在 Vero-76 细胞 (CC50 ≥ 100 μM) 中均表现出低细胞毒性,同时对 EV-A71 表现出显着的选择性。 [10.21203/rs.3.rs-10512011/v1]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The review concludes that human stem cell-derived cultures, organoids, air-liquid interface systems, and assembloids have significantly improved the study of NPEV pathogenesis by mimicking human tissue architecture, cellular complexity, and host responses. [10.1128/jvi.01699-25]

The primary and mature forms of miR-3156-1 were upregulated following enterovirus D68 infection. miR-3156-3p was found to directly target the 3'-untranslated regions of K+ channel-associated genes, leading to plasma membrane depolarization and Ca2+ influx, which increased viral release. [10.1016/j.ymthe.2026.09.038]

CID 101282068, extracted from Diospyros montana, showed predicted binding affinity with docking scores of −9.8 kcal/mol and Gbind = −33.27 kcal/mol. It also maintained the highest number of persistent hydrogen bonds with critical residues at the oligomerization interface. [10.3390/biophysica6050096]

Testing is encouraged to help track disease trends and prevent outbreaks.

papers.title: Beyond polio: advanced human in vitro models for studying non-polio enterovirus pathogenesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT While efforts to eradicate poliovirus are ongoing, non-polio enteroviruses (NPEV) continue to pose a substantial public health threat. NPEVs cause a wide range of diseases, from mild self-limiting infections to severe respiratory, neurological, and cardiac complications, with the highest burden occurring in children and immunocompromised populations. Recent advances in human stem cell-derived cultures, organoids, air-liquid interface systems, and assembloids have transformed the study of NPEV pathogenesis by providing physiologically relevant models that recapitulate human tissue architecture, cellular complexity, and host responses. In this review, we discuss how these advanced in vitro systems have enhanced our understanding of the determinants of viral tropism, including receptor usage, epithelial polarity, tissue-specific susceptibility, and viral genetic variation. We further highlight insights into serotype-dependent differences in innate immune responses, tissue injury, and dissemination mechanisms. Finally, we explore the potential of these models for antiviral discovery and personalized therapeutic development, emphasizing their value for advancing both fundamental and translational NPEV research.

papers.title: Targeting the miR-3156-3p/K+ channel axis suppresses viral release and paralysis in enterovirus D68 infection.
papers.abstract: Viruses rely on egress machinery to exit cells, a step that is crucial for their transmission. While non-enveloped RNA viruses, such as enteroviruses, are typically associated with the lytic release pathway, emerging evidence suggests they can also be packaged within vesicles for non-lytic release. However, the molecular mechanisms that regulate viral release remain unclear. Here, we performed a genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screen in A549 cells and identified the microRNA hsa-miR-3156-1 as a critical host factor for enterovirus infection. Both the primary and mature forms of miR-3156-1 were upregulated following infection, with miR-3156-3p acting as a positive regulator of viral infection by directly targeting the 3'-untranslated regions of the K + channel-associated genes KCNV1, KCNJ2, KCNK3, and KCNK5, thereby causing plasma membrane depolarization and Ca 2+ influx, which increase viral release. Pre-administration of a miR-3156-3p antagomir alleviated virus-associated acute flaccid paralysis in an ICR neonatal mouse model. Our findings reveal how the miR-3156-3p/K + channel axis controls enterovirus release, highlighting potential prophylactic targets.

papers.title: Discovery of oxochromanyl–naphthoquinone hybrids as a new chemotype of selective Enterovirus A71 inhibitors
papers.abstract: Abstract Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is a major causative agent of hand, foot, and mouth disease and is associated with severe neurological complications for which effective antiviral therapies remain unavailable. Inspired by the documented antiviral properties of both naphthoquinone and chromone-based scaffolds, we designed and synthesized a focused library of oxochromanyl–naphthoquinone hybrids through a tandem Michael addition–decarboxylation strategy. The resulting compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity and antiviral activity against a panel of RNA viruses, including EV-A71, coxsackievirus B5 (CVB5), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2. All derivatives exhibited low cytotoxicity in Vero-76 cells (CC50 ≥ 100 μM), while showing a remarkable degree of selectivity toward EV-A71. Structure–activity relationship analysis revealed that antiviral activity was retained across multiple substitution patterns, with several analogues displaying submicromolar potency, indicating that inhibition is a general feature of the oxochromanyl scaffold rather than a feature of a single compound. Several derivatives displayed submicromolar antiviral activity, with compound 3k emerging as the most potent analogue, exhibiting an EC50 value of 0.1 ± 0.01 μM and an estimated selectivity index of approximately 1000. Yield-reduction assays confirmed a dose-dependent suppression of viral production, resulting in a reduction of infectious virus titers of approximately two orders of magnitude. Furthermore, virucidal and time-of-addition experiments demonstrated that the antiviral activity of 3k is not associated with direct virion inactivation but is consistent with interference during the earliest stages of the EV-A71 replication cycle. Collectively, these findings identify oxochromanyl–naphthoquinone hybrids as a previously unexplored class of selective EV-A71 inhibitors and establish the oxochromanyl scaffold as a promising platform for the development of new anti-enteroviral agents.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop new antiviral agents targeting Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), a virus associated with severe neurological complications. The researchers designed and synthesized a library of oxochromanyl–naphthoquinone hybrids, inspired by the antiviral properties of naphthoquinone and chromone scaffolds. The compounds were tested against EV-A71 and other RNA viruses, revealing low cytotoxicity and high selectivity for EV-A71. Structure–activity relationship analysis showed that antiviral activity is a general feature of the oxochromanyl scaffold, with compound 3k demonstrating submicromolar potency. Virucidal and time-of-addition experiments indicated that the antiviral activity of 3k occurs during the early stages of EV-A71 replication. These findings identify oxochromanyl–naphthoquinone hybrids as a new class of selective EV-A71 inhibitors, offering a promising platform for future anti-enteroviral drug development. The study's results are supported by direct experimental evidence, though the findings are limited to the specific compounds tested and their effects on EV-A71.

papers.title_zh: 发现氧代色满基-萘醌杂合体作为选择性肠道病毒 A71 抑制剂的新化学型
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) is a major causative agent of hand, foot, and mouth disease and is associated with severe neurological complications for which effective antiviral therapies remain unavailable. Inspired by the documented antiviral properties of both naphthoquinone and chromone-based scaffolds, we designed and synthesized a focused library of oxochromanyl–naphthoquinone hybrids through a tandem Michael addition–decarboxylation strategy. The resulting compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity and antiviral activity against a panel of RNA viruses, including EV-A71, coxsackievirus B5 (CVB5), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2. All derivatives exhibited low cytotoxicity in Vero-76 cells (CC50 ≥ 100 μM), while showing a remarkable degree of selectivity toward EV-A71. Structure–activity relationship analysis revealed that antiviral activity was retained across multiple substitution patterns, with several analogues displaying submicromolar potency, indicating that inhibition is a general feature of the oxochromanyl scaffold rather than a feature of a single compound. Several derivatives displayed submicromolar antiviral activity, with compound 3k emerging as the most potent analogue, exhibiting an EC50 value of 0.1 ± 0.01 μM and an estimated selectivity index of approximately 1000. Yield-reduction assays confirmed a dose-dependent suppression of viral production, resulting in a reduction of infectious virus titers of approximately two orders of magnitude. Furthermore, virucidal and time-of-addition experiments demonstrated that the antiviral activity of 3k is not associated with direct virion inactivation but is consistent with interference during the earliest stages of the EV-A71 replication cycle. Collectively, these findings identify oxochromanyl–naphthoquinone hybrids as a previously unexplored class of selective EV-A71 inhibitors and establish the oxochromanyl scaffold as a promising platform for the development of new anti-enteroviral agents.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 肠道病毒 A71 (EV-A71) 是手足口病的主要病原体,并与严重的神经系统并发症相关,目前尚无有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法。受萘醌和色酮支架已记录的 抗病毒药物 特性的启发,我们通过串联迈克尔加成-脱羧策略设计并合成了氧代苯并二氢吡喃基-萘醌杂化物的重点库。评估了所得化合物对一组 RNA 病毒的细胞毒性和 抗病毒药物 活性,包括 EV-A71、柯萨奇病毒 B5 (CVB5)、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2。所有衍生物在 Vero-76 细胞 (CC50 ≥ 100 μM) 中均表现出低细胞毒性,同时对 EV-A71 表现出显着的选择性。结构-活性关系分析表明,抗病毒药物 活性在多种取代模式中得以保留,几种类似物显示出亚微摩尔效力,表明抑制是氧代苯并二氢吡喃基支架的一般特征,而不是单一化合物的特征。几种衍生物表现出亚微摩尔级的 抗病毒药物 活性,其中化合物 3k 成为最有效的类似物,其 EC50 值为 0.1 ± 0.01 μM,估计的选择性指数约为 1000。产量减少测定证实了病毒产生的剂量依赖性抑制,导致传染性病毒滴度降低了大约两个数量级。此外,杀病毒和添加时间实验表明,3k 的 抗病毒药物 活性与直接病毒粒子灭活无关,但与 EV-A71 复制周期最早阶段的干扰一致。总的来说,这些发现将氧代苯并二氢吡喃基-萘醌杂化物确定为一类先前未经探索的选择性 EV-A71 抑制剂,并将氧代苯并二氢吡喃支架建立为开发新型抗肠道病毒药物的有前景的平台。

papers.title: Through Bioinformatics, Can an Extract from Diospyros montana Offer Broad-Spectrum Inhibition Against EV-A71 2C Protein?
papers.abstract: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71), belonging to the Picornaviridae family, is the primary causative agent of hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in children under five years of age, and no specific broad-spectrum antiviral therapy is currently available. Despite having extensive research on the EV-A71 3C protease, another nonstructural protein, the 2C protein, which is a highly conserved protein and a member of the ATPases Associated with diverse cellular Activities (AAA+) helicase family, lacks conclusive details of its mechanism. This study, thereby, performed a comprehensive analysis of the wild-type EV-A71 2C protein by studying the role of Zn2+ in structural stability and determining the binding site with two pronounced inhibitors—fluoxetine 12b and dibucaine 6i—as the positive controls via the blind docking method. Then, a virtual screening on a Vietherb database (5071 metabolites from Vietnamese natural sources) yielded 20 top-ranked compounds, which were selected for further molecular dynamics (MD) simulation and cross-variant evaluation. Among these, CID 101282068 extracted from Diospyros montana exhibited overall good, predicted binding affinity (docking score of −9.8 kcal/mol and Gbind = −33.27 kcal/mol) and sustained the highest number of persistent hydrogen bonds with critical residues at the oligomerization interface. Further validation against 23 EV-A71 2C variants highlights its hypothetical broad-spectrum characteristics and can be considered a promising lead candidate targeting EV-A71 2C multimers.

Further validation against 23 EV-A71 2C variants highlights its hypothetical broad-spectrum characteristics and can be considered a promising lead candidate targeting EV-A71 2C multimers.

On the left is a 3D rendering of enterovirus D68 (viral proteins are colored red, yellow, blue) with human monoclonal antibody EV68-228 (orange/purple); to the right of it/in the background is a colorized transmission electron micrograph of enterovirus D68 virus particles (colored in green). Source: NIAID/CDC/Public Domain. What Is AFM? AFM is a rare but serious neurologic condition that causes paralysis and primarily affects children. The condition is characterized by acute onset of flaccid weakness in one or more limbs and spinal cord gray matter abnormalities. AFM is indistinguishable clinically and radiologically from paralytic poliomyelitis caused by poliovirus. The condition has been associated with EV-D68. Related Content CDC Tracking Emergence of Highly Divergent SARS-CoV-2 Variant BA.3.2 A newly released CDC report details the early detection and surveillance of BA.3.2, a highly divergent SARS-CoV-2 ... Urine LAM Assay Shows Promise for Diagnosing TB in Children A new urine-based lipoarabinomannan (LAM) assay demonstrated strong diagnostic performance for tuberculosis in ... Infant Formula Device Linked to Legionnaires Disease Case Legionnaires disease was identified in an immunocompromised infant who had recently consumed powdered formula ... What Are We Doing About It? Nationwide AFM surveillance began in 2014, when an increase in cases was first recognized. EV-D68 circulation was associated with biennial peaks in AFM cases in 2014, 2016, and 2018, when 120 to 238 cases were reported annually. During 2020 through 2025, however, confirmed AFM cases remained lower, ranging from 17 to 48 cases per year. The CDC received reports of 172 confirmed cases during the six-year period: 34 in 2020, 29 in 2021, 48 in 2022, 19 in 2023, 25 in 2024, and 17 in 2025. Although sentinel respiratory surveillance identified increases in EV-D68 detections in respiratory specimens from children with acute respiratory illnesses in 2022, 2024, and 2025, they were not accompanied by concurrent increases in AFM cases nationally. EV-D68 was detected in one specimen from a patient with AFM in 2025. “These findings indicate that increases in EV-D68–associated respiratory illnesses do not necessarily result in increases in AFM cases,” Gabe Alvarado, a CDC spokesperson, told Infectious Disease Special Edition. “Although EV-D68 is considered the primary cause of the peaks in AFM cases observed in 2014, 2016, and 2018, questions remain about the relationship between EV-D68 circulation and AFM,” Alvarado said. “During 2020-2025, increases in EV-D68–associated respiratory illnesses were not accompanied by increases in AFM cases. Additional research is needed to better understand this pattern, including whether changes in circulating EV-D68 strains or other factors may influence the risk for AFM.” What Are the Limitations? The investigators noted that additional AFM patients during the study period might have had EV-D68 infection, but viral detection can be limited by the timing of specimen collection. Specimens from patients with AFM are often collected after the onset of limb weakness rather than during the preceding illness, when viral detection may be more likely. Among patients with confirmed AFM and documented receipt of any polio vaccine doses, 75% to 100% annually were reported to be up to date with polio vaccination. However, only about half of patients had stool specimens collected and tested for poliovirus. In 2022, a case of paralytic poliomyelitis in an unvaccinated person in New York was identified through testing of stool specimens collected through AFM surveillance. The Importance of Surveillance “The report also underscores the importance of continued AFM surveillance,” Alvarado said. “Because AFM can present similarly to paralytic poliomyelitis, surveillance supports timely detection and evaluation of patients with acute flaccid weakness or paralysis and strengthens U.S. polio preparedness. Continued surveillance also provides critical information to improve understanding of AFM epidemiology and monitor trends over time.” Clinicians should remain alert for patients suspected of having AFM, report cases to local or state health departments, obtain polio vaccination status, and collect stool specimens from patients with acute onset of flaccid weakness or paralysis, the CDC said. Alvarado reported no relevant financial disclosures. news.content: Three viruses are rampant in Boise. As of Wednesday, Sept. 30, levels of enterovirus D68 , a respiratory virus that can lead to paralysis, remained " high" in Boise's wastewater , according to the WasterWater Scan dashboard. COVID-19 and norovirus have been trending upward in the Boise area for at least 21 days, according to the dashboard. Both diseases have now reached "high levels" indicating an increase in infections . All three illnesses can have deadly consequences. Here's what Boise-area residents should know: Three viruses show a “high” presence in Boise wastewater. What is enterovirus D68? Enterovirus D68 is a virus that can cause "mild to severe respiratory illness," the CDC said. Infections from EVD68 and other non-polio enteroviruses are most common in the summer and fall, but you can get sick year-round, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. ​​Non-polio enteroviruses cause 10 to 15 million infections and tens of thousands of hospitalizations each year in the United States, the CDC said. "The virus can be found in an infected person's respiratory secretions," the CDC said. This includes saliva and mucus. Infection most likely spreads through coughs, sneezes and by touching surfaces that have come into contact with those who carry the virus. What are symptoms of ED68? In mild cases, symptoms of enterovirus D68 include runny nose, sneezing, cough and body and muscle aches, according to the CDC. "Serious symptoms may include wheezing, difficulty breathing, or pneumonia," the federal health agency said. Severe infections can lead to serious health complications such as pneumonia, encephalitis or meningitis, the Cleveland Clinic said. In the most extreme cases, EVD68 can lead to acute flaccid myelitis, an "uncommon but dangerous neurological condition that mostly affects children," the CDC said. The development of acute flaccid myelitis can cause muscular paralysis , according to the Cleveland Clinic. How common is virus linked to paralysis? Contracting the enterovirus is pretty common , according to the Cleveland Clinic. "In fact, most people over the age of 5 have evidence of a previous infection," the clinic said. Some people show no symptoms at all. SARS-CoV-2 presence spikes in Boise wastewater. COVID-19 infections may be on the rise. How contagious is COVID-19? How does it spread? COVID-19 is a respiratory disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, according to the Mayo Clinic. "It can be very contagious and can spread quickly," the CDC said. The virus that causes COVID-19 "spreads between people in close contact ," the Mayo Clinic said, most commonly through tiny airborne droplets. "When people with COVID-19 cough, sneeze, breathe, sing or talk, their breath may contain the COVID-19 virus," the Mayo Clinic said. How can I tell if I have COVID-19? People with COVID-19 can experience a "wide range" of symptoms , according to the CDC. Many of these are similar to those of the flu, pneumonia or the common cold. According to the Mayo Clinic, signs you have COVID-19 can include: Nausea, vomiting or diarrhea "Symptoms may change with new COVID-19 variants and can vary depending on vaccination status," the CDC said. That's why it's important to get tested for coronavirus in order to receive proper treatment from medical professionals. "Most people with COVID-19 have mild symptoms, but some people can become severely ill resulting in hospitalization or death ," Idaho Department of Health and Welfare said. You do not have to experience symptoms to carry the virus, according to the CDC. WastewaterSCAN data shows “high concentrations” of noroviruses in Boise. Do I have a norovirus infection? Noroviruses are extremely contagious and can produce severe and immediate symptoms. According to the Mayo Clinic, noroviruses are "c ommonly spread through food or water that is contaminated during preparation or through contaminated surfaces. Noroviruses can also spread through close contact with a person who has norovirus infection." Symptoms typically begin with diarrhea, stomach pains, nausea and vomiting and begin within 12 to 48 hours after infection, the Mayo Clinic said. Fevers, headaches and body aches can also accompany main symptoms of noroviruses. Norovirus symptoms can lead to severe dehydration which may require hospitalization, according to the CDC. Signs of dehydration include: Infrequent urination or dark-colored urine Dizziness or being lightheaded Call a doctor or your primary care physician if you have symptoms of a viral infection. What should I do if I'm sick? First and foremost, call your doctor and get tested, according to the CDC. Getting tested helps health officials track disease trends and monitor for potential outbreaks. Children ages 7 and younger, older adults and people with weakened immune systems are most at risk of developing severe symptoms from viral infections caused by COVID, EVD68 and noroviruses, according to the CDC. While there are no known treatments that directly target EVD68 or noroviruses, doctors can attend to some symptoms. If you're sick with the novel coronavirus, there are several antiviral medications that can alleviate symptoms and over-the-counter cold medicines may help as well, according to the CDC. Antiviral medications for COVID-19 such as Paxlovid can interfere with other medications, so talk to your doctor about which treatment plan works best for you. EVD68 and noroviruses don’t have a vaccine to help build immunity against infection. What are ways I can prevent viral infections? " Getting a COVID-19 vaccine helps to keep you healthy," the Mayo Clinic said, protecting "against serious illness, the need for hospital care due to COVID-19 and death from COVID-19." This is especially true for people who are more at risk, including seniors over 65, pregnant people and people with chronic health conditions or weakened immune systems. Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech and Novavax have COVID-19 vaccines available in the United States. There are no specific vaccines approved for EVD68 and noroviruses. People build immunity from enterovirus D68 through exposure over time. "Adults can get infected with enteroviruses, but they are more likely to have no symptoms or mild symptoms," the CDC said. General guidelines for reducing the spread of respiratory infections apply to enterovirus D68, too: Cover your coughs and sneezes Disinfect high-contact surfaces Don't share personal items like drinks, food or clothing Noroviruses can hit hard, fast and multiple times in a row regardless of previous infections. Pay attention to food recall notices and avoid foods that are potentially contaminated with norovirus. Wash foods, surfaces and hands thoroughly before, during and after preparing and consuming meals. Be cautious when consuming raw seafood, especially shellfish. "If eaten raw, oysters and other filter-feeding shellfish can contain viruses and bacteria that can cause illness or death," the CDC said. "Anyone who consumes raw shellfish is at risk of contracting norovirus."

The CDC and Mayo Clinic emphasize that while most people may experience mild symptoms, children, older adults, and those with weakened immune systems are at higher risk for severe outcomes.
